title: Harmonize tokenizers and chat templates in onboarding path
creator: Maya Chen
description: During model onboarding we are seeing frequent compatibility regressions between model tokenizers and the chat/templates used by downstream callers. Symptoms include unexpected tokenization offsets, broken placeholder replacement (e.g., {{user}} / <|endoftext|> mismatches), and degraded perf profiles caused by inconsistent sequence-length estimates. These issues lead to incorrect prompts, truncated responses, and CI failures when publishing performance profiles. This ticket standardizes detection and fixes for tokenizer/chat template compatibility and integrates compatibility metadata into the onboarding and performance profile publishing flow.
problem_statement: Onboarding currently assumes that the model's tokenizer and the runtime chat template are compatible. In practice, tokenizer variants (byte-level vs. unicode-aware, BPE variant differences) and template tokenization edge cases cause: 1) mismatched token counts vs. runtime estimator, 2) escaped or split placeholders, and 3) incorrect padding/attention masks during profiling. We need an automated compatibility shim plus gating checks so published performance profiles and pinned versions are reliable.
goals: 1) Detect tokenizer/template incompatibilities during onboarding. 2) Provide automatic, auditable fixes (normalization rules or shim) where safe. 3) Surface compatibility metadata in model catalog and performance profiles. 4) Prevent publishing profiles unless baseline compatibility checks pass or an explicit opt-in is recorded.
non_goals: Changing user-facing chat template DSL or forcing template migrations across customers; full tokenizer re-training or changing model weights.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a tokenizer compatibility validator in the onboarding pipeline that runs a canonical suite of template + prompt permutations and compares tokenizer tokenization boundaries and counts against the model's expected encoding. 2) Implement a 'template normalization' component that applies deterministic rules (placeholder escaping/unescaping, unicode normalization NFKC, whitespace trimming, canonical placeholder tokens) with a recorded diff. 3) Emit a compatibility status field (compatible | compatible_with_shim | incompatible) into the model metadata and performance profile. 4) Enforce publishing policy: profiles marked 'incompatible' cannot be published; 'compatible_with_shim' requires a short audit note and approver. 5) Add unit and integration tests in onboarding CI and a synthetic workload to validate sequence-length estimators used by the runtime.
implementation_notes: - Reuse tokenization unit tests from runtime/tests/tokenizers. - Add new canonical template corpus (examples covering aggressive emoji/unicode, rich whitespace, braces). - Provide a small fallback shim implemented in Python and the Go runtime: tokenization normalization must produce byte-identical output across both to avoid silent discrepancies. - Add model-metadata fields: tokenizer_name, tokenizer_version, compatibility_status, compatibility_notes, canonicalized_template_hash.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Onboarding pipeline flags compatibility status for every new model in test cluster. 2) For three recent failing models (internal testcases) the shim moves them to 'compatible_with_shim' with recorded diffs and passes automated profile publishing in staging. 3) Publishing UI and model catalog show compatibility_status and notes. 4) No regression in token counts between onboarding estimator and runtime for validated models (within 0 token delta for canonical prompts).
testing_plan: - Unit tests for normalization rules. - Integration tests: run onboarding pipeline on a matrix of 20 templates x 10 tokenizer variants and assert compatibility status. - Staging end-to-end: onboarding -> profile publish -> serve a sample prompt, compare token counts and outputs. - Add fuzz tests for placeholder edge cases. - Add monitoring alert if post-publish runtime tokenization mismatch is observed.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + internal canary: run on internal onboarding jobs only. 2) Staging: enable gating checks and require approver for 'compatible_with_shim'. 3) Gradual rollout to hosted onboarding: start with new models only, run compatibility checks but do not block publishing for 2 weeks while collecting metrics. 4) Enforce blocking policy after metrics look good. 5) Teach solutions team the opt-in/approver flow.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: Existing published models retain prior metadata. We will retro-run compatibility checks for high-traffic models and annotate catalog; retro-running does not change published profiles unless a manual opt-in is done. The runtime shim can be disabled per-model via metadata for cases where customers depend on previous behavior.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track: percent_of_new_models_compatible, percent_moved_to_shim, publish_blocked_count, post_publish_mismatch_rate. Create dashboards in Console under 'Onboarding -> Tokenizer Compatibility'. Add alert if post-publish mismatch rate > 0.5% over 24h.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: shim changes could alter observed model outputs subtly. Mitigation: only apply deterministic normalization that preserves semantic text; require approver sign-off for any shim that changes more than 1 token on canonical prompts. Risk: performance cost of normalization in runtime. Mitigation: perform normalization at onboarding and store canonicalized templates and hashes; runtime uses precomputed canonical templates when available.
owner_notes: If we discover tokenizer implementations that intentionally differ (legacy BPE variants), we'll add an explicit compatibility adapter entry in the model catalog instead of expanding the shim. Coordinate with Applied ML for tokenizer metadata extraction.
next_steps: 1) Spike: implement canonical template corpus and run validator locally (owner: Arjun). 2) Add normalization rules RFC and review with Applied ML (owner: Maya). 3) Ship CI test matrix and add gating in staging (owner: Eng Onboarding squad).
